jobs.title: DevOps Engineer | Live Entertainment Company
jobs.description:
GT  was founded in 2019 by a former Apple, Nest, and Google executive.  GT’s mission is to connect the world’s best talent with product careers offered by high-growth companies in the UK, USA, Canada, Germany, and the Netherlands. 
 On behalf of our client, an international company in the live entertainment industry, GT is looking for an experienced  DevOps Engineer  

  About the Client   
 Our client is one of Europe’s leading live entertainment companies, known for producing large-scale musicals and operating high-traffic ticketing platforms across multiple countries. 
 The company operates a complex internal technology landscape connecting key business systems, marketing, ticketing, and other internal platforms. 
 The Integration Specialist will help strengthen the company’s core digital infrastructure by taking ownership of business-critical integrations, with an initial focus on Boomi-powered integration flows. 

  About the Role  
  Commitment:  Full-time, long-term  Working hours:  European time zone  Start : ASAP 
 We are looking for a DevOps Engineer to build and run Azure platforms on a hub-and-spoke network design, with AKS and container workloads. You will work alongside a platform lead and product development teams, from infrastructure as code to application delivery. 
 The applications you will support are primarily built with PHP and React. You do not need to write application code, but experience building, containerizing, and deploying PHP and Node.js/React applications is a strong plus. 

  Responsibilities:  
 
 
 Build and maintain Azure infrastructure as code using Terraform. 
 
 
 Build and operate hub-and-spoke networks with secure, private connectivity between services. 
 
 
 Run AKS clusters and containerized workloads in production. 
 
 
 Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps. 
 
 
 Deliver applications to Kubernetes using GitOps workflows. 
 
 
 Configure edge routing, ingress, and security: DNS, TLS certificates, and basic WAF/gateway setups. 
 
 
 Set up monitoring, centralized logging, and proactive alerting. 
 
 
 Implement identity and security baselines: Managed Identities, Azure RBAC, secrets management, and policies. 
 
 
 Collaborate on architectural discussions: review technical proposals, surface operational risks, and contribute to runbooks and design records. 
 
 
 Support development teams day to day: local development workflows, Dockerfiles, and debugging in shared environments. 

 
 
  Essential knowledge, skills & experience:  
  1. Azure Core & Platform  
 
 
  3+ years  in DevOps or platform engineering, with at least  2 years supporting Azure in production . 
 
 
 Strong understanding of Azure resource hierarchy: Management Groups, Subscriptions, Resource Groups, and naming/tagging conventions. 
 
 
 Identity & access management: Microsoft Entra ID, Azure RBAC, and Managed Identities. 
 
 
 Hands-on experience with core resources: Storage Accounts (Blob/Files), Key Vault, Azure Container Registry (ACR), and Log Analytics. 
 
 
  2. Infrastructure as Code & Automation  
 
 
  Terraform:  writing modular code, managing remote state, handling multiple environments, and understanding state locking. 
 
 
 Scripting & OS fundamentals:  Linux ,  Bash , and  PowerShell . 
 
 
 Version control with  Git . 
 
 
  3. Containers & Kubernetes  
 
 
  Containers:  building, optimizing, and debugging Dockerfiles; local setups using Docker Compose. 
 
 
  AKS in Production:  cluster provisioning, node pools, autoscaling, ingress controllers, and upgrades. 
 
 
  Kubernetes Operations:  core workload manifests (Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets), Helm chart usage, and troubleshooting via kubectl.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer - Compute Capacity
jobs.description:
About  Supabase   
 Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. 

  About the Role  
 We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there. 
 You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room. 
 You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage. 

  What You'll Be Responsible For  
 
 
 Help build and maintain the capacity plan that keeps Supabase's compute supply ahead of demand across regions and instance families 
 
 
 Support buffer policy by modeling headroom targets and their cost tradeoffs for review and sign-off 
 
 
 Build and maintain automation that turns the capacity plan into provisioned reality — reservation acquisition and top-up, fleet reconciliation, drift detection between committed and running capacity 
 
 
 Extend our infrastructure as code for capacity-relevant provisioning 
 
 
 Instrument capacity: build and maintain metrics for saturation, reservation coverage, idle buffer, forecast error, and provisioning latency 
 
 
 Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact 
 
 
 Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet 
 
 
 Contribute to mitigation projects: right-sizing, instance-family migrations, autoscaling improvements, workload consolidation 
 
 
 Help drive down compute cost per database through right-sizing, placement, and commitment coverage work 
 
 
 Participate in capacity incident response and post-incident follow-through 
 
 
  You Might Be A Good Fit If You  
 
 
  Have 5+ years  across infrastructure engineering, SRE, platform, or capacity engineering, ideally at SaaS or cloud infrastructure scale 
 
 
 Have production software engineering experience —  you've owned and operated a service , not just a notebook. Comfortable in modern languages like  TypeScript, Python , and  Go  
 
 
 Are comfortable working against forecasts and assumptions that are incomplete, and can revise your work as those assumptions change 
 
 
 Have experience with  Infrastructure as Code  (Pulumi or Terraform) 
 
 
 Have built or maintained  observability  for systems you own — metrics that answer real questions and alerting people trust (Prometheus/Grafana, CloudWatch, or similar); 
 
 
 Have solid working knowledge of  AWS EC2 : instance families and generations, purchase options, capacity reservations, and quota mechanics 
 
 
 Have some financial fluency — you understand reservation economics and the basic tradeoffs between coverage, utilization, and cost 
 
 
 Communicate clearly across audiences, from engineers to finance stakeholders 
 
 
  What We Offer  
 
 
  Fully Remote  
 We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. 
 
 
  ESOP

Are you ready to unlock intelligence?  
 If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others. 

  Senior Technical Product Marketing Manager, Agent Identity & Auth (EMEA)  
  Location:  EMEA 

 About the Role: 
 As enterprises move from AI experiments to production agentic systems, a new problem has emerged: agents are non-human actors that need identity, authentication, and authorization — and the traditional identity stack wasn't built for them. 
 This role owns Kong's story in one of the most important emerging categories in AI infrastructure. As Senior Technical PMM for Agent Identity & Auth, you'll define how the market understands agent identity: how agents are authenticated, what they're authorized to access, and how enterprises establish trust and accountability across autonomous systems. 
 This is a category-shaping role. You'll build the narrative for a market that's still being defined, with the opportunity to establish Kong as the definitive voice on non-human identity in agentic architectures. 

 What You'll Do: 
 
 
  Own positioning and messaging for agent identity and auth  — Define the technical narrative for how Kong authenticates, authorizes, and governs agents and other non-human actors across AI and API traffic. 
 
 
  Shape the category  — Develop thought leadership that frames the agent identity problem for the market and establishes Kong's point of view through blogs, talks, analyst conversations, and industry engagement. 
 
 
  Lead technical field enablement  — Own enablement in this domain for Kong Solution Engineers, Customer Success Managers, and other technical field roles. 
 
 
  Produce deep technical content  — Build demos, reference architectures, technical whitepapers, and documentation-adjacent content that helps architects and security teams evaluate and adopt Kong's approach. 
 
 
  Support strategic deals  — Serve as the subject-matter expert for sales conversations where agent identity and security are strategic decision criteria, particularly with security and platform engineering buyers. 
 
 
  Fuel launches and campaigns  — Deliver technical positioning, proof points, and demo assets as structured inputs to the AI PMM's launch and campaign motions. 
 
 
  Partner with product management  — Inform roadmap framing and capability naming based on market feedback, competitive dynamics, and buyer research. 
 
 
 What You'll Bring: 
 
 
 5+ years of experience in product marketing, product management, or solutions engineering -ideally at an Identity and Access Management (IAM) and/or AI Security company. 
 
 
  A genuine, hands-on interest in AI infrastructure. You follow developments in LLM deployment, agentic frameworks, the Model Context Protocol, and AI governance, and can speak credibly to AI platform engineers without bluffing.  
 
 
 A proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into crisp narratives that land with both technical practitioners and C-suite buyers. 
 
 
 Highly collaborative -you thrive working across Product, Marketing, Sales, and Partner teams. 
 
 
 Comfortable owning a stage: keynote presentations, analyst briefings, customer roundtables, and demo-heavy sessions energize you rather than intimidate you. 
 
 
 Experience in open-source software, SaaS platforms, and enterprise go-to-market motions is strongly preferred. 
 
 
 Familiarity with the AI connectivity landscape -including awareness of competing and complementary vendors across API gateways, AI observability, vector databases, iPaaS, and agentic orchestration frameworks - is a strong plus.
